metadata.methods_description: EEG was recorded at 250 Hz with a 74-channel Easycap passive Ag/AgCl cap, amplified by a MEGIN TRIUX system and referenced to the mastoids. Stimulus presentation and online feedback were run with BCI2000. Each trial had a 1 s inter-stimulus interval followed by a 5 s target presentation, with cursor feedback from 3 to 6 s. The protocol specified 32 trials per run.

citation_details.title: Neural mechanisms of training in Brain-Computer Interface : A Biophysical modeling approach
citation_details.author: Apurba Debnath, Tristan Venot, Marie‐Constance Corsi, Parul Verma
citation_details.abstract: Abstract Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) is a system that translates neural activity into commands, allowing direct communication between brain and external devices. Despite its clinical application, BCIs are unable to robustly capture subjects’ intent due to limited understanding of the neural mechanisms underlying BCI control. To address this, we introduce a biophysical linear neural mass model to investigate the associated neural mechanisms of motor imagery BCI (MI-BCI) by modulating the scale-free spectral characteristics of afferent inputs. We tailor this motor imagery neural mass model (mi-NMM) to simulate both MI and resting-state activity and apply it to a cohort of 19 healthy subjects trained over four sessions, during which magnetoencephalography and electroencephalography signals were simultaneously recorded. citation_details.title: Brain Network Dynamics from Neuronal Avalanches for Longitudinal Motor-Imagery Decoding
citation_details.author: Camilla Mannino, Alice Longhena, Mario Chávez, Marie‐Constance Corsi
citation_details.abstract: ABSTRACT Brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) offer opportunities for personalized neurorehabilitation, but inter-session variability, repeated calibration, and the need for expert supervision limit their use beyond supervised settings. We propose a longitudinal BCI framework that integrates neuronal avalanches dynamics, reflecting cascades of propagation neural activity, with graph-theory and data-driven region of interest analysis to extract computationally efficient and neuro-physiological interpretable features. Source-reconstructed EEG from 20 BCI-naïve participants performing right-hand motor imagery (MI) and rest across four training sessions was represented by a directed weighted connectivity network based on neuronal avalanches. Local, mesoscopic, and global network measures revealed task-related changes predominantly in contralateral sensorimotor regions and distributed reorganization across training.
